::: {.notes}
Jordan — business case (about 40 seconds). High-end watch prices reflect craftsmanship, scarce production and collector demand. Auction houses and the secondary market offer observable prices, but two prestigious houses may represent a selective, higher-end clientele. Our question is not what to buy automatically: it is which Rolex, Cartier or Omega auction lots merit a closer look. The five available pre-auction inputs are brand, normalized model, case body, movement and age. We propose a 10% margin over the catalogue estimate midpoint for an initial flag; this has not been optimized. A flag triggers a roughly two-minute review. At higher volume, test a 20% margin to reduce review burden.
:::

::: {=html}
<div class="watch-slide">
<div class="eyebrow">AII 600 · Luxury watch auction valuation · Original model & experiments · 0:40–1:30</div><h1 class="section">Why the five-feature booster won</h1><p class="lead">2024 tests favored GBQR; changing model class mattered more than adding listing features.</p><div class="two" style="grid-template-columns:1.28fr .72fr"><div class="chartbox"><div class="charttitle">2024 chronological validation · n = 802</div><div class="fine">Mean dollar pinball loss · lower is better</div><div class="barrow"><span>Brand q33</span><div class="track"><div class="fill base" style="width:97.4%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">$4,380.90</b></div><div class="barrow"><span>Linear q33</span><div class="track"><div class="fill base" style="width:88.3%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">$3,975.74</b></div><div class="barrow"><span>CatBoost</span><div class="track"><div class="fill base" style="width:73.8%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">$3,321.24</b></div><div class="barrow"><span>IQN</span><div class="track"><div class="fill base" style="width:71.3%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">$3,207.60</b></div><div class="barrow"><span>GBQR</span><div class="track"><div class="fill" style="width:70.4%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">$3,168.73</b></div></div><div class="card"><div class="kicker">Compared with linear</div><div class="metric">−20.30%</div><p class="metriclabel">$807.01 less mean pinball per watch — <b>not money saved</b></p><div style="height:15px"></div><div class="kicker">Feature experiments</div><p class="small">Tested extra-feature bundles did not improve overall loss; box and papers may matter for rare, high-value pieces.</p></div></div><p class="fine" style="margin-top:15px">IQN was close ($38.87 higher); the date-clustered bootstrap did not establish a clear advantage. Trained through 2023; validated on 2024.</p><div class="foot"><span>Conservative valuation · Rolex / Cartier / Omega</span><span>2 / 4</span></div>
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Jordan introduces the original model; Speaker 3 presents comparisons (about 50 seconds total). Overestimating value is costlier than overlooking a deal because capital tied up in a bad purchase is hard to recover. We chose a 2:1 penalty rather than 3:1, which could be excessively cautious. This implies a 33rd-percentile prediction, not a purchase probability. Models used the same five basic inputs. On the chronological 2024 validation set of 802 lots, GBQR dollar pinball loss was $3,168.73 versus $3,975.74 for linear q33: 20.30% lower. IQN was close and not decisively worse. Tested feature bundles added little overall, although box and papers could matter greatly for specific rare watches. A separate rebuild yielded worse results; its cause is not established.
:::

<div class="eyebrow">AII 600 · Luxury watch auction valuation · Validation & risks · 1:30–2:15</div><h1 class="section">A better score is not a guarantee</h1><p class="lead">Only 23.80% of 2026 sales fell at or below predicted q33, versus the 33.33% target.</p><div class="two" style="grid-template-columns:1.2fr .8fr"><div class="chartbox"><div class="charttitle">2026 observed share at or below predicted q33</div><div class="fine">Expected target: 33.33%</div><div class="barrow"><span>Target</span><div class="track"><div class="fill base" style="width:83.3%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">33.33%</b></div><div class="barrow"><span>All watches</span><div class="track"><div class="fill" style="width:59.5%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">23.80%</b></div><div class="barrow"><span>Cartier</span><div class="track"><div class="fill" style="width:53.3%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">21.31%</b></div><div class="barrow"><span>Omega</span><div class="track"><div class="fill" style="width:78.5%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">31.39%</b></div><div class="barrow"><span>Rolex</span><div class="track"><div class="fill" style="width:53.5%"></div></div><b style="text-align:right">21.40%</b></div></div><div class="card"><div class="kicker">Separate 80% prediction interval</div><div class="metric">78.43%</div><div class="metriclabel">2024 coverage</div><div style="height:15px"></div><div class="metric">72.65%</div><div class="metriclabel">2026 coverage</div><p class="fine">$650.96 adjustment learned from 2023 only; q33 unchanged.</p></div></div><p class="notice" style="margin-top:18px">GBQR still had lower 2026 pinball ($5,540 vs. $6,538), but its low q33 may distort screening flags. The later window is not an untouched test set.</p><div class="foot"><span>Conservative valuation · Rolex / Cartier / Omega</span><span>3 / 4</span></div>
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Speaker 3 — strongest challenge (about 45 seconds). We should not confuse low dollar pinball loss with reliable probabilities or investment returns. In 2026, only 23.80% of prices fell at or below the GBQR predicted q33 versus a 33.33% target. Separate 80% interval coverage fell from 78.43% in 2024 to 72.65% in 2026. The data come from two high-end auction houses and may not generalize to ordinary dealer transactions. Auction prices can reflect premiums, market cycles, condition and provenance. A different objective, such as stricter calibration or fewer manual reviews, could change our model choice.
:::

::: {=html}

::: {.notes}
Anya — conclusion (about 45 seconds). On 762 comparable 2024 lots, GBQR and linear q33 disagreed on 203 review flags: 139 GBQR-only and 64 linear-only. This shows that model selection changes analyst workload, not proven profit. We would rank candidates by potential upside and review them manually for authenticity, condition, provenance, transaction costs and resale liquidity. The 10% margin is a starting point, not a validated optimal threshold; at scale we would compare 10% and 20% based on review capacity and missed opportunities. Revisit the recommendation if fresh data erase the loss advantage, calibration is critical, or verified transaction economics change the decision. Each team member should be ready to defend the choice, rejected alternative, strongest check, and what would change it.
:::
